_note: Premium variant text, weapons pass (director 2026-11-15: unique text for every variant the way Hemathorn and Weeping Testament were done; faithful replacement of the parent's text to suit each variant's theme and style). Each entry mirrors its parent item's description and battleDescription sentence by sentence, swapping imagery to the variant and keeping the weapon's effects in the battle line. Parent text read live 2026-11-15. Consumed by push/620_variant_text_weapons.gen.py.

variants.name: Windward
variants.description: A blade made from wind and lantern fire, a thread of skyglass down its fuller and its grip wrapped in old sailcloth. It burns like a deck lamp on the long watch.
variants.battleDescription: %user pulls out a blade bound in sailcloth and releases their dual-nature fire and wind chakra. The skyglass thread catches like a lantern wick, the flame leaning with the wind. %user then launches the blade at %target, cutting clean through and leaving the wound smouldering like a doused deck.

variants.name: The First Blade
variants.description: A blade made from wind and fire chakra in the First Blade's colours, his gale cord bound tight around the grip. It sat bored for decades. Not any more.
variants.battleDescription: %user pulls out a blade wound in the First Blade's gale cord and releases their dual-nature fire and wind chakra. The cord snaps taut and a cold blue flame runs to the tip, eager after decades of waiting. %user then launches the blade at %target, cutting clean through, and the flame keeps burning in the cut.

variants.name: Thunderwake
variants.description: A blade of lightning caught in skyglass, said to have been cut from the war-ship's masthead storm-rod in the middle of a gale.
variants.battleDescription: %user pulls out a katana with a storm-rod set into its crossguard, releasing a strong current through the blade. The skyglass hums like a masthead in a squall and glows white-blue, and, as if the storm had followed them aboard, %user slashes at %target. Thunder keeps ringing in the wound, and every blow after it lands harder.

variants.name: Wayfinder
variants.description: A blade of lightning steered by a skyglass compass rose, said to have held a heading through the storm the Wayfinder never came back from.
variants.battleDescription: %user pulls out a katana, releasing a strong current through the blade. The compass rose in the guard swings and settles on %target, the etched heading lighting down the fuller, and, as if the storm had found its course, %user slashes at %target, marking them for every blow that follows.

variants.name: Rotbloom
variants.description: Used to reap what the Core grew wrong.  Rotten rope chain with cloudy skyglass blooms  Each bloom = one memory gone sour  Spreads where it cuts  Not every harvest is meant to be eaten.
variants.battleDescription: %user twirls the Rotbloom above their head and sends it toward %target, the rotten rope coiling around them. %user pulls it back, the cloudy skyglass blooming in the wound as it rips a chunk of flesh from %target and drags them closer.

variants.name: Anchorline
variants.description: Used to call the crew back to their posts.  Black chain with skyglass beads  Each bead = one name on the duty roster  Tightens when a post is abandoned  Not everyone who answers is still alive.
variants.battleDescription: %user swings the Anchorline above their head and casts it toward %target like a dropped anchor, the chain wrapping around them. %user hauls it back, every bead on the roster ringing as it rips a chunk of flesh from %target and drags them to their post.

variants.name: Stargazer
variants.description: Silent ranged navigation tool.  Bow limbs etched with the Wayfinder's chart lines in skyglass, corrected and corrected again  Arrows hold a heading only the bow can see  No wind, no drift  Victims fall exactly where the chart said they would
variants.battleDescription: %user forms a pale bow traced with skyglass chart lines, using their chakra as the string and drawing an arrow tipped with starlight. They sight along the corrected heading and loose it directly at %target, and the stolen light runs back up the string into %user.

variants.name: The Remainder
variants.description: Silent ranged erasure tool.  Bow limbs gone matte and still  Arrows leave no wounds, only absence  No light, no glint  Victims fall as if the world forgot they were there
variants.battleDescription: %user forms a bow gone matte black and still, its chakra string never once catching the light. They draw an arrow that drinks the light around it and release it at %target, the dust hanging unmoving where it passed, and what it took flows back into %user.

variants.name: The Unwritten Order
variants.description: Nobody knows what it says.  The mission line is left blank  Opens only when an order is about to be given  Seals itself again in cyan wax
variants.battleDescription: %user snaps open a fan of unwritten orders, its blank mission line glowing beneath cyan wax, and sweeps it across the battlefield. The order lands on %target before anyone can read it, and it takes what it is owed.

variants.name: Captain's Gunbai
variants.description: Everybody knew what it meant.  Black lacquer with a skyglass star at its heart  Raised only when an order would not be repeated  Lowered when the deck fell silent
variants.battleDescription: %user raises the Captain's Gunbai, the skyglass star at its heart catching the light, and brings it down across the battlefield like a command. The order breaks over %target and tears away what they were holding onto.

variants.name: Heartglass
variants.description: Everybody knows whose it is.  Paned in cyan Mother Glass  Opens only when a name is about to be remembered  Never quite closes
variants.battleDescription: %user opens Heartglass, its panes of Mother Glass ringing like a held breath, and sweeps it across the battlefield. The crystal heart flares, and the light cuts into %target, drawing out what they had left and keeping it.

variants.name: Keelstone
variants.description: <b><i>A long spear forged around a shard of the wreck's keel, its shaft banded in ship's iron like a hull held together by rivets. A skyglass crystal glows at the tip, still carrying the weight of the whole ship, making it a weapon that will not break.
variants.battleDescription: %user channels their chakra into the spear, and the keel shard at its tip hardens like a hull meeting rock before they drive it into %target, staving in their defenses and leaving them listing.

variants.name: Skyglass Kote
variants.description: A pair of raw skyglass sleeves, cut whole from the wreck and left unpolished. They're lightweight, but harder than the hull, and they gleam even in the dark of the hold.
variants.battleDescription: %user punches at %target with a fist of raw skyglass, the shards along the sleeve biting in and leaving every technique after it harder to hold together.

variants.name: Forgefists
variants.description: A pair of forge-blackened gauntlets with maul-head knuckles, seamed with cooled skyglass. They're heavy, they're still warm, and the Foundry Warden never set them down.
variants.battleDescription: %user drives a forge-hot fist into %target like a maul on an anvil, the skyglass seams flaring, and the heat left in the blow makes every technique after it cost more to shape.

variants.name: Lastlight Duskblade
variants.description: A blade of pure silver around a heart of skyglass that glows like the Lastlight Lantern. It absorbs the chakra around it and burns it low and steady, pointing home, before letting it go in one long swipe.
variants.battleDescription: %user raises the Duskblade as its skyglass heart draws in the chakra around them like a lantern gathering the last of the light, then swings it down across %target in a single dusk-coloured swipe.

variants.name: Skysail
variants.description: A fan with a skyglass crystal set at its heart, its ribs strung like the war-ship's sails. It has a unique ability to catch the wind and turn it into blades.
variants.battleDescription: %user swings their fan like a sail coming about, catching the wind in its rigging and loosing it as blades that slice into %target, leaving long gashes that keep stinging like salt spray.

variants.name: Hullbreaker
variants.description: A large axe on a haft of ship's timber, skyglass set into the cheek of the head and imbued with the cold of the deep water beneath the wreck. It has opened a few hulls.
variants.battleDescription: With each hit from the axe, %target splits like a hull on the rocks, and a frost of cold seawater seeps from the wounds.

variants.name: Sealscript
variants.description: The legendary sword of sealing, written end to end in the Sealwright's script, a skyglass seal at the pommel. It remembers every report he buried.
variants.battleDescription: %user quickdraws, the Sealwright's script lighting down the blade as it slices at %target's vital areas. Line by line the script writes itself into %target, and their chakra is sealed away like a buried report.

variants.name: Riptide
variants.description: A blade cooled in the Foundry's flood and beaded with skyglass down its spine, coated with water that never stops pulling.
variants.battleDescription: %user channels earth chakra to form a blade and then coats it with water drawn from the Foundry's flood. %user taps the blade against %target, and the current along the skyglass beads drags at the point of impact, freezing it as it pulls.

variants.name: Crownbreaker
variants.description: A blade forged from the depths of the earth beneath a broken crown of skyglass, coated with water for a freezing touch no command can thaw.
variants.battleDescription: %user channels earth chakra to form a blade beneath a broken crown of skyglass and then coats it with below-freezing water. %user taps the blade against %target, and the point of impact freezes solid, as if ordered to kneel.

variants.name: Nightreaver
variants.description: “When the lamps go out, this blade keeps watch. When the last one gutters, it remembers.”  Nightreaver is not forged for war, but for the night watch. Its edge is blackened not by fire, but by the hours — each strike counted like a bell rung on deck. The skyglass star at its guard is not decoration; it is the last lamp left lit, burning for every watch that ended without relief.  In Seichi, it is said that:  the blade grows heavier when a post is abandoned,  lighter when the watch is kept,  and will not draw blood until the last lamp is lit.  Those who survive its cut lose the hour. Those who fall stand the watch forever.
variants.battleDescription: %user holds a blade as dark as the hold at midnight, one star of skyglass burning at its guard. With one swift movement, too quick for the naked eye, the blade pierces through %target.
